polygonSection.title: New polygonal cross section
polygonSection.hint: Drag vertices to move them, click an edge midpoint to insert a vertex, double-click a vertex to remove it.
polygonSection.invalidShape: The shape must be a simple polygon with a positive area: no crossing edges, and holes must stay inside the outline.
polygonSection.centroidalNote: All second moments of area are taken about axes through the centroid; I₁, I₂ are the principal values and α is the angle from the y axis to axis 1.
polygonSection.outOfPlaneNote: This section is not symmetric about the frame plane. A 2D analysis is exact only if the member is held against sideways deflection (out of the screen) and twisting along its whole length, for example by a slab or closely spaced bracing; supports at the nodes alone are not enough. A free member also twists because the loads act off its shear centre, and that twist is not included in the deflections.
polygonSection.outOfPlaneRestrained: Held sideways and against twisting along its length: {inertia}
polygonSection.outOfPlaneFree: Free to deflect sideways (twisting still not included): {inertia}

material.alphaT: The coefficient of thermal expansion describes how the size of an object changes with a change in temperature.
material.e: Young's modulus measures the tensile or compressive stiffness when the force is applied lengthwise.
material.g: The shear modulus is a property that measures resistance to deformation under shear stress, indicating the material's stiffness in response to forces applied parallel to its surface.
material.density: Density is a measure of how much mass is contained in a given volume of a substance.

menu.title: Menu
menu.description: Open, save and share your projects, export an image, load an example, or start this tour or the first-beam task again.

undoRedo.title: Undo and redo
undoRedo.description: Step back and forward through your changes. Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z do the same.

viewerControls.title: Viewer buttons
viewerControls.description: The viewer controls are the way to center or fit the structure to screen, and to select what to display.

viewerSettings.title: Customize Display Options
viewerSettings.description: Choose what to display – be it normal force, shear force, bending moment, deformed shape, or everything together.

gridUnits.title: Grid, snapping and units
gridUnits.description: G shows the grid and S snaps new nodes to it. Click the units to change them, the language or the coordinate system.

bottomBar.title: Add, remove & modify entities
bottomBar.description: The central hub where every aspect of your structure can be effortlessly transformed. From nodes to elements, loads, materials, and cross-sections, it's the go-to place for swift and comprehensive changes.

help.title: Help
help.description: The ? explains the tab you have open. The ? next to a column heading explains that column.

tool.title: Pick the drawing tool
tool.body: In the {elementsTab} tab below, press the {addElement} button with the cursor icon.

draw.title: Draw the beam
draw.body: Click where the beam starts, then where it ends. The ends snap to the grid.

supports.title: Support it
supports.body: Click the left end, open {defineSupports} and tick Dx and D{v} for a pinned support. Then click the right end and tick D{v} for a roller.

load.title: Load it
load.body: Click the beam, choose {addLoad}, enter a value in f{v} and confirm.

display.title: Choose what's shown
display.body: The cog at the top right opens the display options: internal forces, deformed shape, reactions and more. Open it now.

fit.title: Fit it to the screen
fit.body: The buttons at the top right fit the model to the screen or center it. Press fit to screen now, and again whenever the drawing drifts out of view.

results.title: Read the results
results.body: The bending moment and deformed shape are drawn on the beam and update as you edit. Every node, element and load is also listed in the tables below, where you can type exact values. {undo} brings back the model you had before.

solveDiagnostics.summaryIncomplete: {count} parts of the structure need supports.
solveDiagnostics.blockedDescription: Fix the listed errors before solving the model.
solveDiagnostics.warningsDescription: The model was solved, but the following warnings were detected.
solveDiagnostics.incompleteDescription: Results appear once the structure is held in place. The dashed outline on the canvas shows how it can still move.

issues.elementSameNode: Element {element} references the same node at both ends.
issues.supportedNodeNotConnected: Node {node} is supported but no element connects to it, so the support carries nothing.
issues.nodeNotConnected: Node {node} is not connected to any element and is ignored by the solver.
issues.insufficientSupports: Model needs at least 3 constrained DOFs to be stable in 2D analysis.
issues.needsSupports: The structure needs supports before it can be solved.
issues.partUnsupported: A separate part of the structure (nodes {nodes}) has fewer than 3 restrained DOFs and can move freely.
issues.partNeedsSupports: The part with nodes {nodes} needs supports.
issues.mechanism: Structure has enough supports but they do not hold it: it can still {motion}. Supports that are all parallel, or whose lines of action meet in one point, leave the structure free to move.
issues.mechanismShort: The supports do not hold the structure: it can still {motion}.
issues.partMechanism: A separate part of the structure (nodes {nodes}) has enough supports but they do not hold it: it can still {motion}. Supports that are all parallel, or whose lines of action meet in one point, leave the structure free to move.
issues.partMechanismShort: The part with nodes {nodes} is not held: it can still {motion}.
issues.hingeMechanism: The supports hold the structure, but it is still a mechanism: its members can turn about the hinges at node {nodes}. Remove a hinge, or add a member or a support that stops the motion.
issues.hingeMechanismShort: The hinges at node {nodes} let the structure move.
issues.unstable: Structure is unstable: {dofs} moves practically without resistance. Add a support or an element, remove an end hinge, or check the cross section stiffness.
issues.unstableShort: The structure is unstable: it moves almost without resistance.
issues.singularMatrix: Structure is a mechanism: the stiffness matrix is singular. Check that every part is held by at least 3 restraints and that end hinges do not leave a member free to rotate.
issues.singularMatrixShort: The structure is a mechanism: it can move without resistance.
issues.solverFailed: Solver failed due to an internal model inconsistency. Please review model references and loads.

warnings.importFailed: Could not import the file. Please check the file format.
warnings.prescribedDisplacementExists: Prescribed displacement already exists for this node. Please remove it first.
warnings.addCrossSectionFirst: Please add a cross section first.

nodes.title: Nodes
nodes.body: Nodes are the points that hold the structure together. Their coordinates, supports, hinges and the loads applied to them are set per node.

supports.title: Supports
supports.body: Tick a degree of freedom to restrain it: Dx and D{v} block translation, R{r} blocks rotation. A structure needs at least three independent restraints.

elements.title: Elements
elements.body: Elements connect two nodes and carry a material and a cross section. Release an end to turn a beam into a hinged or truss member.

loads.title: Loads
loads.body: Loads act on nodes or along elements. Positive values follow the global axes, with z pointing down.
loads.bodyYUp: Loads act on nodes or along elements. Positive values follow the global axes, with y pointing up.

nodalLoads.title: Nodal loads
nodalLoads.body: A nodal load applies a force or a moment directly to a node. Prescribed displacements let you impose a support settlement instead.

elementLoads.title: Element loads
elementLoads.body: Element loads act along a member: uniform, trapezoidal, concentrated or temperature. They can be given in global or local axes.

materials.title: Materials
materials.body: A material carries Young's modulus, shear modulus, density and thermal expansion. Only E and the section matter for a plain static analysis.

crossSections.title: Cross sections
crossSections.body: A cross section supplies the area and second moment of area used for stiffness. Pick one from the library or draw your own polygon.

hinges.title: End hinges
hinges.body: A ticked box releases the bending moment at that end of the element. Tick both ends to make a truss bar, one end to put a pin inside a frame.

signConvention.title: Sign convention
signConvention.body: Global z points down, so a positive Fz or fz pulls downwards and My is positive counter-clockwise. Loads switched to the local system follow the element instead.
signConvention.bodyYUp: Global y points up, so a positive Fy or fy pushes upwards and Mz is positive counter-clockwise. Loads switched to the local system follow the element instead.

results.title: Results
results.body: Once the model solves you get normal force, shear force, bending moment, deformed shape and reactions, both as diagrams and as tables.

diagrams.title: Result overlays
diagrams.body: These switches draw the normal force, shear force, bending moment, deformed shape and reactions over the model. N is positive in tension, M{r} positive when sagging.

endForces.title: End forces
endForces.body: X12, Z12 and M12 act at the start node, X21, Z21 and M21 at the end node, always in the element's local system running from its initial to its end node.

settings.title: Units & settings
settings.body: Language, units, viewer scale, colors and shortcuts live here. Units convert existing values, they never change the model.

sharing.title: Saving & sharing
sharing.body: Save the model as a file, copy a link that carries the whole structure, or embed a read-only viewer in your own page.

exportImage.title: Export image
exportImage.instructions: The drawing is laid out fresh for the size you pick, so lines and labels keep their real thickness. The same size always frames the structure the same way — handy for exporting M, N and V side by side.
exportImage.pickWindowHint: Drag a rectangle over the drawing to export
exportImage.dragEdge: Drag to reveal or trim this side
exportImage.scaleCaption: 1 m of the model is {cm} cm on paper (96 DPI). Scroll over the preview to zoom.
exportImage.doesNotFit: Not everything fits at this size: the diagrams, loads and labels run about {px} px past the edge. Shrink the diagrams (now {diagrams} px) or enlarge the canvas.
exportImage.shrinkNotEnough: Smaller diagrams are not enough here — the loads and labels alone need more room. Enlarge the canvas instead.
